```text
domain:
    # N: number of samples, M: number of features
    k: dim in [0, N)        # sample index
    j: dim in [0, M)        # feature / column index
    i: dim in [0, M)        # feature / row index for covariance

data:
    # Centered data matrix X of shape [N, M].
    # Layout chosen to match the Noarr definition:
    #   scalar<DATA_TYPE>() ^ vector<'j'>() ^ vector<'k'>()
    # so that j is the innermost (contiguous) dimension and k is outermost.
    data[k, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * M + j
        # row-major: all features j of a given sample k are stored contiguously

    # Per-feature mean vector μ of length M.
    mean[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # contiguous 1D array over j

    # Symmetric covariance matrix Σ of shape [M, M].
    cov[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j
        # row-major: row i contiguous in j

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE      # number of samples as a floating-point scalar, float_n = (DATA_TYPE) N
    N: int                  # number of samples (k dimension size)
    M: int                  # number of features (i and j dimension sizes)

    # Tunable blocking / vectorization parameters
    TILE_K: int             # tile size along k (samples), e.g. 64..512
    TILE_I: int             # tile size along i (covariance rows), e.g. 16..64
    TILE_J: int             # tile size along j (covariance cols), e.g. 16..64
    VEC_I: int              # SIMD width used when vectorizing in i
    VEC_J: int              # SIMD width used when vectorizing in j

computation:
    # 1) Compute per-feature means:
    #    mean[j] = (1 / float_n) * sum_{k=0}^{N-1} data[k, j]

    # Initialize means
    for j:
        mean[j] = (DATA_TYPE)0

    # Accumulate sums over all samples
    for k, j:
        mean[j] += data[k, j]

    # Normalize by float_n
    for j:
        mean[j] /= float_n

    # 2) Center each feature (subtract its mean from every sample):
    #    data[k, j] <- data[k, j] - mean[j]
    for k, j:
        data[k, j] -= mean[j]

    # 3) Covariance:
    #    For 0 <= i <= j < M:
    #      cov[i, j] = (1 / (float_n - 1)) * sum_{k=0}^{N-1} data[k, i] * data[k, j]
    #      cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]  (enforce symmetry)
    for i, j:
        if j >= i:
            cov[i, j] = (DATA_TYPE)0
            for k:
                cov[i, j] += data[k, i] * data[k, j]
            cov[i, j] /= (float_n - (DATA_TYPE)1.0)
            cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]

optimization:
    # Layout:
    #   - Keep `data` and `cov` row-major (j innermost) as above so that traversals with j as
    #     the inner loop naturally stream through contiguous memory.
    #   - This matches the Noarr layouts j_vec ^ k_vec for `data` and j_vec ^ i_vec for `cov`.

    # Step 1 (mean computation):
    #   - Traverse samples k in large tiles to improve cache reuse and parallelize across tiles.
    #   - Within each tile, make j the innermost loop to stream across each row of `data`
    #     and to allow SIMD over features.
    block(k, K_t, TILE_K)              # introduce a tile index K_t over k for mean and centering
    hoist(K_t)                         # K_t outer: process data in k-tiles for good cache reuse
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)                # vectorize accumulation over contiguous features j
    parallelize(K_t)                   # parallelize tiles of k with a reduction into mean[j]
    #   - Parallel reduction over mean[j] can be implemented with per-thread mean buffers
    #     of size M and a final reduction; extra memory is O(#threads * M), typically well
    #     below 50% of the size of `data`.

    # Step 2 (centering):
    #   - Reuse the same (K_t, j) traversal order so that both `data[k, j]` and `mean[j]` are
    #     accessed in a streaming SIMD-friendly pattern.
    #   - No extra directives needed beyond block/hoist/vectorize above.

    # Step 3 (covariance = Xᵀ X / (N-1)):
    #   - Treat the centered data `data` as an N×M matrix X and compute Σ = Xᵀ X / (N-1).
    #   - Use 3D blocking in (i, j, k) so that:
    #       * a TILE_K×TILE_I panel of X (over k×i) and a TILE_K×TILE_J panel of X (over k×j)
    #         fit in L2/L3 cache,
    #       * a TILE_I×TILE_J tile of cov[i, j] fits in registers / L1.
    #   - Only compute the upper triangle (j >= i) inside each tile and mirror to the lower
    #     triangle to preserve symmetry without redundant work.

    block(i, I_t, TILE_I)              # tile covariance rows
    block(j, J_t, TILE_J)              # tile covariance columns
    block(k, Kb, TILE_K)               # tile sample dimension for covariance accumulation

    hoist(I_t)                         # outermost: independent row-tiles of cov
    hoist(J_t)                         # then column-tiles within each row-tile
    hoist(Kb)                          # innermost tile along k: accumulate partial dot-products

    vectorize(i, VEC_I)                # vectorize across i within a (I_t, J_t, Kb) tile
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)                # and/or across j, depending on micro-kernel design

    parallelize(I_t)                   # parallelize across disjoint row-tiles of cov[i, j]
    # On many-core systems, optionally also:
    # parallelize(J_t)                 # 2D tiling of Σ; each (I_t, J_t) tile is independent.

    # Implementation note:
    #   Within each (I_t, J_t, Kb) tile, accumulate into a small temporary TILE_I×TILE_J
    #   buffer held in registers or stack memory and write it back to `cov` after the Kb-loop.
    #   For reasonable tile sizes this extra storage is << 50% of the full covariance matrix
    #   and greatly improves cache locality and SIMD utilization.
```

```text
domain:
    # N = number of samples, M = number of features
    k: dim in [0, N)          # sample index
    j: dim in [0, M)          # feature index (column)
    i: dim in [0, M)          # feature index reused as row for covariance

data:
    # data: N x M, sample-major row-major
    #   layout matches: scalar<num_t>() ^ vector<'j'>() ^ vector<'k'>()
    #   i.e. tuning.data_layout = j_vec ^ k_vec
    #   => 'k' is outer, 'j' is inner, so each sample's feature vector is contiguous
    data[k, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * M + j

    # mean: M-vector over features, contiguous
    mean[j]: inout DATA_TYPE   = (j) -> j

    # cov: M x M covariance matrix, row-major in (i, j)
    #   layout matches: scalar<num_t>() ^ vector<'j'>() ^ vector<'i'>()
    #   i.e. tuning.cov_layout = j_vec ^ i_vec
    #   => 'i' is outer, 'j' is inner
    cov[i, j]: out DATA_TYPE   = (i, j) -> i * M + j

parameters:
    # Integer problem sizes (from defines.hpp / set_length)
    N: int                     # number of samples  (length in k)
    M: int                     # number of features (length in j and i)

    # Floating parameters
    float_n: DATA_TYPE = (DATA_TYPE) N
    inv_n: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE = 1.0 / (float_n - (DATA_TYPE)1.0)

    # Tunable blocking and SIMD parameters (chosen per target HW)
    TI: int    # tile size for i (cov rows)
    TJ: int    # tile size for j (features / cov cols)
    TK_mean: int    # tile size for k in the mean computation
    TK_center: int  # tile size for k in centering step
    TK_cov: int     # tile size for k (reduction dim) in covariance
    VW: int         # SIMD vector width (elements processed together along the inner dim)

computation:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 0) Initialization (init_array):
    #    data[k, j] = (k * j) / M
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    init_data:
        for k, j:
            data[k, j] = (DATA_TYPE)(k * j) / (DATA_TYPE)M

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) Compute per-feature means:
    #
    #    mean[j] = (1 / N) * sum_{k=0..N-1} data[k, j]
    #
    #    Original code:
    #      traverser(data, mean).for_dims<'j'>(...)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    mean_compute:
        for j:
            mean[j] = inv_n * sum(k, data[k, j])

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) Center data in-place:
    #
    #    data[k, j] <- data[k, j] - mean[j]
    #
    #    This matches the original second loop nest.
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    center_data:
        for k, j:
            data[k, j] = data[k, j] - mean[j]

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Covariance matrix:
    #
    #    After centering, for all i, j with j >= i:
    #       cov[i, j] = (1 / (N-1)) * sum_k data[k, i] * data[k, j]
    #       cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]    # enforce symmetry explicitly
    #
    #    This matches the original implementation that:
    #      - iterates i, j
    #      - skips j < i
    #      - reduces over k
    #      - then writes cov[j, i] = cov[i, j].
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    cov_compute:
        for i, j:
            if j >= i:
                cov[i, j] = inv_n_minus_1 * sum(k, data[k, i] * data[k, j])
                cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]

dependencies:
    # Initialization must complete before any kernel work
    for k in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        init_data(k, j) -> mean_compute(j)

    # Means must be available before centering
    for k in [0, N), j in [0, M):
        mean_compute(j) -> center_data(k, j)

    # Centered data must be available before covariance accumulation
    for k in [0, N), i in [0, M), j in [0, M) with j >= i:
        center_data(k, i) -> cov_compute(i, j)
        center_data(k, j) -> cov_compute(i, j)

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Keep data sample-major row-major:
    #   data[k, j]: (k, j) -> k * M + j
    # so that, for fixed k, iterating over j is contiguous.
    # This is exploited in centering and in a GEMM-like
    # covariance accumulation (see below).

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 1: mean[j] = inv_n * sum_k data[k, j]
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Use feature blocking and parallelization along j,
    # while iterating k in the inner loop for good reuse of
    # each sample row in cache.
    #
    # Loop structure after blocking (conceptual):
    #   for J_mean in tiles of j with size TJ (possibly in parallel):
    #       for j in J_mean: mean[j] = 0
    #       for k in [0, N):
    #           for j in J_mean: mean[j] += data[k, j]
    #       for j in J_mean: mean[j] *= inv_n
    #
    block(j, J_mean, TJ)
    # no need to block k here; each sample row is streamed once
    parallelize(J_mean)         # each thread handles a tile of features independently
    vectorize(j, VW)            # SIMD across features within a sample row

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 2: centering data[k, j] -= mean[j]
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Centering is memory-bound and fully independent across k.
    # Use blocking to operate on cache-friendly tiles of (k, j),
    # and parallelize across tiles in k.
    #
    # Preferred loop structure:
    #   for K_c in tiles of k with size TK_center (in parallel):
    #       for k in K_c:
    #           for j in [0, M):
    #               data[k, j] -= mean[j]
    #
    block(k, K_center, TK_center)
    block(j, J_center, TJ)
    hoist(K_center)             # outermost: distribute k-tiles across cores
    parallelize(K_center)       # threads get disjoint ranges of samples
    vectorize(j, VW)            # contiguous along j within each sample row

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Stage 3: covariance on centered data:
    #    cov[i, j] = inv_n_minus_1 * sum_k data[k, i] * data[k, j]
    #    for j >= i, then symmetrize.
    #
    # This is mathematically equivalent to:
    #    C = (1 / (N-1)) * X^T X
    # where X is the centered data matrix (N x M).
    # So we apply GEMM-style blocking in (i, j, k).
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block i, j, k:
    block(i, I, TI)             # tiles of cov rows
    block(j, J, TJ)             # tiles of cov cols
    block(k, K_cov, TK_cov)     # tiles of samples (reduction dimension)

    # Traverse tiles in GEMM-like order: I (rows), then J (cols),
    # then K_cov (sample blocks). Within a (I, J, K_cov) tile,
    # update a TI x TJ sub-block of cov using TK_cov samples.
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K_cov)

    # Parallelization:
    # - Each (I, J) tile of the upper triangle (j >= i) is independent.
    # - For each such tile, the thread also writes the symmetric
    #   entries cov[j, i], so no other thread touches those cells.
    parallelize(I)              # distribute row-tiles across cores

    # Vectorization and unrolling:
    # - Vectorize across j within a row tile so that cov[i, j..j+VW-1]
    #   are updated together using SIMD instructions.
    # - Unroll the k-loop inside each tile to expose ILP and use FMA.
    vectorize(j, VW)
    unroll(k, 4)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Optional temporary buffer for improved data reuse in cov:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # To reduce memory traffic in cov_compute further, we can
    # allocate a per-thread temporary buffer row[j] of length M:
    #
    #   for each k-block K_cov:
    #       for k in K_cov:
    #           # Load one sample row contiguously
    #           for j in [0, M):
    #               row[j] = data[k, j]
    #           # Use row[] repeatedly to update the (I,J) tile:
    #           for i in I:
    #               for j in J with j >= i:
    #                   cov[i, j] += row[i] * row[j]
    #
    # This makes each centered sample value read from memory only
    # once per sample, with O(M) extra storage per thread, which
    # is negligible compared to O(N*M) and stays well below the
    # allowed 50% memory overhead.
```

```text
domain:
    # N: number of samples, M: number of features
    k: dim in [0, N)      # sample index
    j: dim in [0, M)      # feature index (for mean, data columns, cov columns)
    i: dim in [0, M)      # feature index (for cov rows)

data:
    # Raw sample matrix X, modified in-place to hold centered data.
    # Layout matches the Noarr choice j_vec ^ k_vec: k is the fastest dimension.
    #
    #   X[k, j] at address base_X + (k + j * N)
    #
    X[k, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k + j * N

    # Per-feature mean (size M), laid out contiguously.
    mean[j]: out DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

    # Covariance matrix (M x M), with i as the fastest dimension (row-major).
    #
    #   cov[i, j] at address base_cov + (i + j * M)
    #
    cov[i, j]: out DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i + j * M

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE              # N cast to DATA_TYPE (number of samples)
    inv_n: DATA_TYPE                # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE        # = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # Tunable tile sizes and vectorization / unrolling factors
    Ti_cov: int                     # tile size for i in covariance
    Tj_cov: int                     # tile size for j in covariance
    Tk_cov: int                     # tile size for k in covariance
    VF_mean: int                    # vectorization factor for k in mean computation
    VF_cov: int                     # vectorization factor for k in covariance
    U_cov: int                      # unroll factor for k in covariance

computation:
    # 1) Compute feature means:
    #
    #    mean[j] = (1 / N) * sum_{k=0..N-1} X[k, j]
    #
    #    This uses the *uncentered* input X.
    for j:
        mean[j] = inv_n * sum(k, X[k, j])

    # 2) Center data in-place:
    #
    #    X[k, j] ← X[k, j] - mean[j]
    #
    #    After this, X holds centered data and is no longer needed in its original form.
    for j:
        for k:
            X[k, j] = X[k, j] - mean[j]

    # 3) Covariance matrix:
    #
    #    For centered data X (samples along k, features along j),
    #    cov[i, j] = cov[j, i] = (1 / (N - 1)) * sum_k X[k, i] * X[k, j].
    #
    #    We exploit symmetry by computing only the upper triangle (j >= i)
    #    and mirroring it to the lower triangle.
    for i:
        for j:
            if j < i:
                # lower-triangular entries are filled by symmetry elsewhere
                skip
            else:
                acc = sum(k, X[k, i] * X[k, j])
                cov[i, j] = inv_n_minus_1 * acc
                if j > i:
                    cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]    # enforce symmetry

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Data layout choices
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # X[k, j] uses k as the fastest-varying dimension (k-contiguous),
    # which matches the dominant inner loops that reduce over k in both
    # mean computation and covariance. This is encoded via the affine
    # address expression (k + j * N) in the data section.
    #
    # cov[i, j] uses i as the fastest-varying dimension (i-contiguous),
    # which is convenient when iterating over pairs (i, j) with i as the
    # inner index inside 2D tiles.

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic simplifications
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Precompute reciprocals to replace per-element divisions:
    #   inv_n         = 1.0 / float_n
    #   inv_n_minus_1 = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)
    # and use multiplication by these instead of repeated division.
    # This is already reflected in the computation section.

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean and centering (Steps 1 and 2)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Outer loops over j are independent across features, so we can
    # process different j in parallel.
    parallelize(j)              # for loops over full j in mean and centering

    # Inner reductions over k in mean computation are good vectorization
    # candidates, since they are simple, stride-1 loops over X[k, j].
    vectorize(k, VF_mean)       # vectorize mean[j] accumulation over k

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Covariance (Step 3) — dominant cost
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Treat the covariance as a symmetric rank-k update:
    #
    #   cov = (1 / (N - 1)) * X^T * X
    #
    # where X is N x M (samples x features). We block the loops over i, j, k
    # to increase cache reuse, especially reusing X[k, *] and X[* , *] across
    # neighboring (i, j) pairs within a tile.
    #
    # Block i, j, and k; introduce tile dimensions I_cov, J_cov, K_cov.
    block(i, I_cov, Ti_cov)
    block(j, J_cov, Tj_cov)
    block(k, K_cov, Tk_cov)

    # Hoist tile loops to the outermost levels so that computation proceeds
    # over tiles first, then over intra-tile indices.
    hoist(I_cov)
    hoist(J_cov)
    hoist(K_cov)

    # Parallelize across tiles in the i-dimension (and optionally also J_cov).
    # Each (i, j) pair is owned by exactly one tile with j >= i, and that tile
    # is responsible for writing both cov[i, j] and cov[j, i], so there are no
    # write races between threads.
    parallelize(I_cov)

    # Vectorize and unroll inner reductions over k inside each (i, j) pair:
    #   cov[i, j] += sum_{k in K_tile} X[k, i] * X[k, j]
    # where k is stride-1 for both X[k, i] and X[k, j].
    vectorize(k, VF_cov)
    unroll(k, U_cov)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Triangular structure
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each (I_cov, J_cov) tile:
    #   - Restrict work to (i, j) pairs with j >= i; skip (i, j) where j < i.
    #   - After computing cov[i, j], copy it to cov[j, i] when j > i.
    #
    # This preserves the original program’s behavior (compute only the
    # upper triangle and mirror it) while avoiding redundant arithmetic.
```

domain:
    # N: number of samples, M: number of features  (N = float_n, M = data | get_length<'j'>())
    k: dim in [0, N)         # sample index
    i: dim in [0, M)         # feature index (row of covariance)
    j: dim in [0, M)         # feature index (column of covariance)

data:
    # Raw / centered data matrix X: shape N x M
    # Store row-major so all features of a sample k are contiguous.
    X[k, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * M + j
        # initially: X[k,j] = data[k,j]
        # after centering: X[k,j] = data[k,j] - mean[j]

    # Feature means: length M
    mean[j]: out DATA_TYPE = j

    # Covariance matrix: shape M x M, stored row-major (i-major, j-minor)
    cov[i, j]: out DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE                 # number of samples N (float_n = (DATA_TYPE) N)
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE             # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE           # = 1.0 / (float_n - (DATA_TYPE)1.0)

computation:
    # 1) Compute column means: mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_k X[k,j]
    MEAN_INIT:
        for j:
            mean[j] = 0

    MEAN_ACCUM:
        for j:
            mean[j] += sum(k, X[k, j])

    MEAN_SCALE:
        for j:
            mean[j] *= inv_float_n

    # 2) Center data in place: X[k,j] <- X[k,j] - mean[j]
    CENTER_DATA:
        for k, j:
            X[k, j] -= mean[j]

    # 3) Covariance (upper triangle) and symmetry
    #    cov[i,j] = sum_k X[k,i] * X[k,j] / (N - 1),  for j >= i
    COV_UPPER:
        for i, j:
            if j >= i:
                cov[i, j] = inv_n_minus_1 * sum(k, X[k, i] * X[k, j])

    #    enforce symmetry explicitly: cov[j,i] = cov[i,j]
    COV_SYMMETRIZE:
        for i, j:
            if j > i:
                cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # Layout and scalar precompute
    # -----------------------------
    # X:
    #   - keep row-major (k-major, j-minor) so all features of a sample k
    #     are contiguous in memory.
    #   - this favors per-sample outer-product style covariance updates
    #     and streaming passes over X.
    #
    # cov:
    #   - row-major (i-major, j-minor) so inner loops over j write
    #     contiguous elements.
    #
    # Scalars:
    #   - precompute inv_float_n and inv_n_minus_1 once to avoid
    #     repeated divisions inside inner loops.

    # -----------------------------
    # 1) Mean computation
    # -----------------------------
    # Base computation is per-column: mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_k X[k,j].
    # For locality on row-major X, we transform to a streaming form
    # over k (rows) with j as innermost, and use a reduction for mean.

    # Transform MEAN_ACCUM to:
    #   for k:
    #     for j:
    #       mean[j] += X[k,j]
    #
    # This streams X row-by-row and keeps mean[] hot in cache.
    MEAN_ACCUM:
        interchange(j, k)

        # Parallelization:
        #   - mean[j] is independent across j, but we now iterate (k outer, j inner).
        #   - Implement a parallel reduction in k with per-thread partial sums:
        #       mean_t[thread, j] = sum_{k in thread_chunk} X[k,j]
        #     then reduce mean[j] = sum_thread mean_t[thread, j].
        #   - At the model level, express that k-iterations are parallelizable
        #     under a reduction on mean.
        parallelize(k)  # # with a reduction on mean over k

        # Vectorization:
        #   - j is the innermost, contiguous dimension; vectorize over j.
        vectorize(j, VEC_J_MEAN)  # VEC_J_MEAN: tunable SIMD width for mean pass

    # -----------------------------
    # 2) Centering X
    # -----------------------------
    # CENTER_DATA currently: for k, j: X[k,j] -= mean[j]
    # This already streams X row-major and repeatedly reuses mean[j].

    CENTER_DATA:
        # Parallelize across rows: each (k, :) row is updated independently.
        parallelize(k)

        # Vectorize across the contiguous feature dimension j.
        vectorize(j, VEC_J_CENTER)  # often = VEC_J_MEAN

    # Optionally, fuse CENTER_DATA with MEAN_SCALE:
    #   for j: mean[j] *= inv_float_n
    #   for k,j: X[k,j] -= mean[j]
    # This keeps mean[j] hot and reduces mean's cache traffic.
    # (Kept as a comment-level hint; functional behavior unchanged.)

    # -----------------------------
    # 3) Covariance computation
    # -----------------------------
    # Mathematically:
    #   cov = inv_n_minus_1 * X^T X   (after centering)
    #
    # The base model uses:
    #   cov[i,j] = inv_n_minus_1 * sum_k X[k,i]*X[k,j] for j >= i,
    #   cov[j,i] = cov[i,j].
    #
    # Optimization goals:
    #   - Maximize reuse of rows X[k,:] so each sample row is loaded
    #     as few times as possible.
    #   - Tile in (i,j,k) to fit into caches and allow parallelism
    #     over covariance blocks.
    #   - SIMD over the innermost contiguous feature dimension.

    COV_UPPER:
        # 3D tiling of (i, j, k).
        # TI, TJ, TK are tunable tile sizes chosen to fit L2/L3 caches.
        block(i, I, TI)   # I: tile index over rows of cov
        block(j, J, TJ)   # J: tile index over columns of cov
        block(k, K, TK)   # K: tile index over samples

        # Hoist tile loops outermost so we iterate tiles in (I,J,K) space:
        #   for I, J with J >= I (upper tiles):
        #     for K:
        #       for (i in tile I, j in tile J with j >= i):
        #         accumulate over k in tile K
        hoist(I)
        hoist(J)
        hoist(K)

        # Skip strictly-lower-triangular tiles:
        #   - tiles with J < I contain only (i,j) with j < i, which are never used
        #     as primary covariance sites (we fill them from cov[j,i]).
        #   - only process tiles with J >= I; for diagonal tiles, enforce j >= i
        #     within the tile; for off-diagonal (J > I), process all (i,j) in the tile.
        #   (This is a semantic restriction on the (I,J) iteration domain.)

        # Within each (I,J,K) tile:
        #   - stream over K (sample blocks), loading TK rows X[k,:].
        #   - for each k in K, load the sub-vectors:
        #       X[k, i in I-block] and X[k, j in J-block]
        #     and perform an outer-product update into the cov tile.
        #
        # Parallelization:
        #   - Different (I,J) tiles update disjoint cov submatrices; they
        #     have no write–write races and can be computed in parallel.
        parallelize(I, J)

        # Vectorization:
        #   - Within a tile, choose j as the innermost contiguous dimension
        #     in the inner loops updating cov[i,j] so that:
        #        for i in I-block:
        #          for j in J-block:
        #            cov[i,j] += sum_{k in K-block} X[k,i]*X[k,j]
        #     can be vectorized over j.
        vectorize(j, VEC_J_COV)

        # Optional unrolling of the K-tile for better ILP when TK is small.
        unroll(K, UNROLL_K_COV)

    COV_SYMMETRIZE:
        # Symmetrization writes each off-diagonal pair twice:
        #   cov[j,i] = cov[i,j]   for j > i.
        # These writes are independent across (i,j) pairs.
        parallelize(i, j)

        # Since cov is row-major, making j the innermost loop
        # allows vectorized stores on cov[j,i] across contiguous j.
        vectorize(j, VEC_J_SYM)

    # -----------------------------
    # Summary of tunable parameters
    # -----------------------------
    # TI, TJ, TK       : tile sizes for i, j, k in covariance accumulation
    # VEC_J_MEAN       : SIMD width for mean accumulation along j
    # VEC_J_CENTER     : SIMD width for centering along j
    # VEC_J_COV        : SIMD width for covariance inner j-loop
    # VEC_J_SYM        : SIMD width for symmetrization inner j-loop
    # UNROLL_K_COV     : unroll factor for K-tile loop in covariance

    # These parameters are chosen so that:
    #   - additional temporary storage per thread (for partial means and tile-local
    #     accumulators, if implemented) remains well below 50% of the size of X;
    #   - tile working sets fit into target cache levels on the x64 machine.

```text
domain:
    # N: number of samples, M: number of features
    k: dim in [0, N)      # sample index
    j: dim in [0, M)      # feature index / covariance column
    i: dim in [0, M)      # covariance row index

data:
    # Centered data matrix X (samples × features).
    #  - Initially contains raw samples.
    #  - After centering, contains X_c[k,j] = X[k,j] - mean[j].
    #  - We choose a "samples-major" layout (k contiguous) so that all k-reductions
    #    in the kernel iterate over stride‑1 memory.
    data[k, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> j * N + k
        # j is the slow dimension (feature), k is the fast dimension (sample).

    # Covariance matrix cov[i,j] (M × M), symmetric.
    #  - We keep classical row-major layout (rows i, columns j) so that for each i
    #    we sweep j consecutively.
    cov[i, j]: out DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j

    # Per-feature mean.
    mean[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = j -> j

parameters:
    N: size_t                 # number of samples, equals length in k
    M: size_t                 # number of features, equals length in j and i
    float_n: DATA_TYPE        # = (DATA_TYPE)N
    inv_n: DATA_TYPE          # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE  # = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

computation:
    # 1) Compute per-feature means:
    #    mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_k data[k,j]
    for j in [0, M):
        acc_mean = 0.0
        for k in [0, N):
            acc_mean += data[k, j]
        mean[j] = acc_mean * inv_n

    # 2) Center data in-place:
    #    data[k,j] <- data[k,j] - mean[j]
    for j in [0, M):
        mj = mean[j]              # hoist mean[j] out of inner loop
        for k in [0, N):
            data[k, j] -= mj

    # 3) Covariance from centered data:
    #    cov[i,j] = cov[j,i] = (1/(N-1)) * sum_k data[k,i] * data[k,j]
    for i in [0, M):
        for j in [i, M):          # upper triangle including diagonal
            acc = 0.0
            for k in [0, N):
                acc += data[k, i] * data[k, j]
            cov[i, j] = acc * inv_n_minus_1
            cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]  # enforce symmetry

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # Data-layout and arithmetic
    # -----------------------------
    # - Use the samples-major layout chosen in 'data' for 'data[k,j]':
    #     address = j * N + k
    #   With this, all k-loops in the kernel (mean, centering, covariance)
    #   traverse contiguous memory and are amenable to SIMD.
    #
    # - Precompute inv_n and inv_n_minus_1 once instead of dividing inside
    #   the inner loops:
    #     mean[j] = acc_mean * inv_n
    #     cov[i,j] = acc * inv_n_minus_1
    #   This replaces O(M^2) divisions in phase 3 by cheaper multiplications.

    # -----------------------------
    # Tiling / blocking
    # -----------------------------
    # Dominant cost is phase 3: O(M^2 * N). We tile all three dimensions
    # (i, j, k) to improve cache reuse and reduce bandwidth.
    #
    # Tiling for phases 1–3:
    block(i, I, TI)     # i = I * TI + i_in,    TI: tile size in covariance rows
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J * TJ + j_in,    TJ: tile size in covariance cols / features
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K * TK + k_in,    TK: tile size in samples (reduction dim)

    # Loop-nest order for the covariance kernel:
    #   for I
    #     for J  (restricted to J >= I to honor j >= i)
    #       allocate small local tile cov_tile[TI, TJ]
    #       cov_tile[:] = 0
    #       for K
    #         # accumulate over TK samples into cov_tile
    #       scale cov_tile by inv_n_minus_1
    #       write cov_tile back to cov[i,j] and its symmetric counterpart
    #
    hoist(I)            # outermost: tiles of covariance rows
    hoist(J)            # next: tiles of covariance columns
    hoist(K)            # then tiles of samples (reduction dimension)

    # Within each (I,J,K) tile:
    #  - Keep k_in as the innermost loop (stride-1 in 'data' because k is fast).
    #  - Accumulate partial sums into a small register / stack-resident tile
    #    cov_tile[TI, TJ] to avoid repeated loads/stores of cov[i,j].
    #    This uses O(TI * TJ) extra memory per thread, which is negligible
    #    (well under +50% of the original footprint for reasonable TI,TJ).
    vectorize(k, VK)    # SIMD over k_in inside each tile
    unroll(k, UK)       # optional unrolling factor for k_in

    # -----------------------------
    # Parallelization
    # -----------------------------
    # Phases 1 and 2:
    #  - Independent across features j. After tiling j -> (J,j_in),
    #    parallelize over J.
    parallelize(J)      # for mean-computation and centering loops

    # Phase 3 (covariance):
    #  - Different (i,j) pairs are independent once data are centered.
    #  - After tiling, parallelize across I (and optionally J) tiles, while
    #    still enforcing that only tiles with J >= I are executed.
    parallelize(I)

    # Tile sizes TI, TJ, TK, and SIMD/unroll factors VK, UK are tunable
    # constants chosen to match the cache hierarchy and SIMD width of the
    # target x64 machine (e.g., TI,TJ ≈ 32–64 for L2, TK chosen so that
    # TI*TJ*TK fits comfortably into L1).
```
